clues.title: Plate: white with blue letters
text: Licence plates are **white** with **blue** letters. The blue sheen of the letters can be hard to see through the blur, and the plates might appear as plain white.
Plates on government vehicles are [green](https://goo.gl/maps/Y5GJLe2TPsuKVnts5).
clues.summary: White plates with blue letters. The blue sheen is hard to see through the blur, so they can look plain white. Government vehicles have green plates.

clues.title: Google car: striped car or ridged antenna
text: On the Generation 3 coverage you can find two different Google cars:
- A car with a short, stubby antenna. The antenna has **three ridges**. It can sometimes be hard to tell if the antenna has ridges.

- A white car with **stripes** and no antenna. There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right. The stripes are sometimes [poorly visible](https://goo.gl/maps/4vGAo6xju653jkXQ9).
The car is not always as visible as shown in the example images.
NOTE: This specific striped white car is unique to Cambodia. Make sure not to mix it up with the [Bangladeshi striped car](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jUkCUxjEsT75EzWf6), which looks slightly different.
The Latin American countries of Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador and Brazil also have cars with similar short antennas. However, these have a diagonally coiled ridge, instead of Cambodia’s three ridges.

images.caption: Red circle highlights the thin ridged antenna above the striped car blur

clues.summary: Gen 3 has two cars: one with a short stubby antenna with three ridges, and a white car with no antenna, a white stripe on the left and a yellow stripe on the right. The striped car is unique here.

differs.how: Bangladesh also has a striped car, but with different stripes

clues.title: Driving side: right
text: Cambodia drives on the **right**.
NOTE: Thailand drives on the left, while Vietnam and Laos also drive on the right.

images.caption: Road with traffic on the right; the yellow sign shows two-way traffic

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the right. Thailand drives on the left, while Vietnam and Laos also drive on the right.

clues.title: Language: Khmer script, curvy and intricate
text: **Khmer **is the official language of Cambodia. It has its own unique script, which is very distinct and recognizable. In most fonts, letters have an intricate, curvy look.
Khmer can look fairly different depending on the font used. A compilation of what this script looks like in street view can be [found here](/images/cambodia/cambo_script.png).
NOTE: The Thai and Lao scripts look similar, but the letters tend to have a less intricate look. However, some simplified Khmer fonts can look a bit like Thai and Lao.
clues.summary: Khmer has its own script with intricate, curvy letters, though fonts vary a lot. Thai and Lao look similar but are less intricate, and simple Khmer fonts can resemble them.

clues.title: Pole: concrete ladder pole or round holed pole
text: Two types of poles are common:
- Concrete** ladder** poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).
- Round concrete poles with small **holes**.
Rarely, you might see simple [wooden poles](https://goo.gl/maps/ffGjZufAA38brtLg6).
NOTE: The same type of round concrete pole is also common in [Vietnam](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mhQRGYEqaoehmkSr6).

You can easily distinguish between Thailand and Cambodia based on the poles. Thailand uses square concrete poles with rows of small pinholes on the sides. Such poles are very uncommon in Cambodia (but not [completely absent](https://goo.gl/maps/6YWqPhcJmHvYEFp78)).

images.caption: Two concrete poles: a ladder pole (left circle) and a round holed pole (right circle)

clues.summary: Two common types: concrete ladder poles with ridges, and round concrete poles with small holes. Rare wooden poles exist. Vietnam has the same round poles. Thailand uses square poles with rows of tiny holes, which are rare here.

differs.how: Thailand uses square concrete poles with rows of tiny pinholes

clues.title: Bollard: red-and-white stone
text: Cambodia has a variety of different **bollards**. The most common ones are:
- A stone bollard with red-and-white stripes.
- A stone bollard with a red top and a white base, usually with a reflector in the red part.
Some bollards are unique to a road or region. More details can be found in the region-guessing section.
clues.summary: Most common are a stone bollard with red-and-white stripes, and a stone bollard with a red top and white base, usually with a reflector in the red part. Some designs belong to single roads.

clues.title: Route marker: stone, white base, red top
text: Cambodian** road markers** are made of stone, with a white-coloured base and a rounded red top. You will find the road number on the narrow side and a town name with a distance on the main side.
clues.summary: Stone road markers with a white base and a rounded red top. The road number is on the narrow side and a town name with distance on the wide side.

clues.title: Chevron: black with yellow arrows
text: Chevrons in Cambodia are **black with yellow arrows**.
Chevrons are somewhat rare. On many occasions, Cambodia prefers to use bollards instead of chevrons to mark curves in the road.
NOTE: Chevrons in all other Southeast Asian countries have the reverse colour scheme: yellow with black arrows.
clues.summary: Curve signs are black with yellow arrows. They are rare, since bollards often mark curves instead. All other Southeast Asian countries use yellow with black arrows, the reverse.

differs.how: Thailand's chevrons are yellow with black arrows

clues.title: Road lines: yellow centre, rare white edge
text: Roads have dashed or solid **yellow middle road lines**. Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.
NOTE: Thailand uses similar road lines.
clues.summary: Dashed or solid yellow centre lines. Edge lines are rare and solid white when present. Thailand uses similar lines.

clues.title: Roads: many are unpaved
text: Many roads are **unpaved**. Usually, only main roads and roads in and near urban areas are paved.
clues.summary: Many roads are unpaved. Usually only main roads and roads in or near towns are paved.

clues.title: Houses: wooden stilt houses, vertical planks
text: **Wooden houses on stilts** are common. Walls are often made of vertical planks. Many homes have [double or triple roofs](https://goo.gl/maps/21wWXJpTT8z9E3ua9).
clues.summary: Wooden houses raised on stilts are common. Walls are often vertical planks and many roofs are double or triple layered.

clues.title: Houses: red-brown or blue walls, blue trim
text: In addition, traditional Cambodian wooden stilt houses tend to have very recognizable **colour schemes**.
- Walls are commonly painted dark red-brown, light blue or an ochre orange.
- Doors, windows and other architectural details are often painted bright blue.
NOTE: More modern houses tend to have a wider variety of colour schemes.
clues.summary: Traditional stilt houses have walls painted dark red-brown, light blue or ochre orange, with bright blue doors and windows. Newer houses use more colours.

clues.title: Houses: orange or red tiled roofs
text: Many traditional homes have **tiled orange or red roofs**, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges and corners. Corrugated and plain metal roofs are also common.
On other, more modern buildings, you can see a wider variety of roof colours and materials.
clues.summary: Many traditional homes have orange or red tiled roofs, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges. Plain or corrugated metal roofs are also common. Newer buildings vary.

clues.title: Buildings: ornate Buddhist temples
text: The majority of Cambodians are **Buddhist**. Temples are common throughout the country. Temple architecture is highly decorative, with ornamented roofs. You might also see [Buddhist flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist_flag).
NOTE: Thailand and Laos are also majority Buddhist. Temples in these countries can look similar.
clues.summary: Most people are Buddhist, so decorated temples with ornamented roofs are common. Thailand and Laos have similar temples.

clues.title: Ads: Angkor, Anchor and Cambodia beer
text: You will see a lot of **advertisements** for the beer brands Angkor, Anchor, and the very creatively named Cambodia Beer.
clues.summary: Lots of adverts for the beers Angkor, Anchor and Cambodia Beer.

clues.title: Sign: blue political party signs
text: Throughout the country, you can find distinct **blue signs** from the Cambodian People’s Party (CPP).
These signs occasionally feature the likenesses of major party politicians: usually [three men](https://goo.gl/maps/uWwgvxjSdKMp7W676) side by side.

images.caption: Large blue party billboard with Khmer script, right

clues.summary: Blue signs from the ruling party across the country, often with three men's faces side by side.

clues.title: Coverage: low-quality brownish camera
text: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Cambodia. This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”). It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours. A good map will not usually include this coverage, but it is good to be aware of its existence, in order to not be caught off-guard by it.
NOTE: Within Asia, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal also have shitcam coverage.
clues.summary: A poor camera with a wide circular car blur and brownish colours. Good maps rarely include it. India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal have the same camera.

clues.title: Coverage: limited, around big cities
text: **Street view coverage** is somewhat limited. Most of the coverage is located around the cities of Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and Battambang.

_You can click on the image to enlarge it. You can also view the official street view coverage in more detail on [this site](https://sv-map.netlify.app/#base=roadmap&cov=official2x&zoom=8&center=12.541158630852788%2C104.71069335937501)._
clues.summary: Street View is patchy. Most of it is around the capital, Siem Reap and Battambang.

clues.title: Coverage: low-quality camera in the southwest
text: Shitcam in Cambodia is only found in the **southwestern** half.
clues.summary: The low-quality camera is only found in the southwestern half of the country.

clues.title: Landscape: flat farmland with villages
text: The **low-lying central plain** is home to most agricultural land. The landscape is flat, cultivated, and dotted with villages and farms.
clues.summary: The low central plain holds most of the farmland: flat, cultivated land dotted with villages and farms.

clues.title: Landscape: wild, uncultivated northeast
text: Conversely, **the northeast** is much more uncultivated: there is less agriculture and more natural vegetation. Some areas are slightly hilly.
clues.summary: In the northeast, there is less farming and more natural vegetation, with some slightly hilly areas.

clues.title: Landscape: hills and low mountains
text: **The southwest** is the area with the most elevation in Cambodia. This region is characterized by hills and low mountains. Some inland roads feature dense forest cover, but the coastal areas in particular are fairly densely populated.
clues.summary: The southwest is the highest part, with hills and low mountains. Inland roads can have dense forest, while the coast is quite densely populated.

clues.title: Soil: sandy white ground
text: **Sandy, white soil** is very common in the region southeast of Phnom Penh, as well as around the city itself. The colour can range from bright white to slightly beige.
NOTE: You may find sandy, white soil in other parts of the country, however it is by far the most common in this area. Conversely, some roads in this region can have darker soil than expected.
clues.summary: Sandy white soil, from bright white to beige, is very common southeast of the capital and around it. It appears elsewhere less often, and some roads here have darker soil.

clues.title: Landscape: mountain ridge to the north, red soil
text: Near the northern border with Thailand, you can often see a **mountainous ridgeline to your north**. The soil in this region tends to be red, ranging from a slight reddish tinge to deep dark red.

The ridgeline closely corresponds with the border with Thailand. The drop-off to the Cambodian lowland to its south is abrupt. This means that the roads you are on are themselves located in a very flat landscape (see inset map).
clues.summary: Near the northern Thai border, a mountain ridge runs along the horizon to your north, with red soil. The road itself is on a very flat lowland below the ridge.

differs.how: Thai side is higher, but looks similar from the border

clues.title: Plants: rubber tree plantations in rows
text: **Rubber tree plantations** are found in three places:
- In a narrow belt northeast of Phnom Penh, mostly centred around the southern sections of Roads 7 and 71
- Around the town of Ban Lung in the far northeast, as well as east of it on and near Road 78.
- Around the town of Pech Sreada. This area has a distinct look. See the tip in the spotlight section.
Rubber trees can be recognized by their thin trunks and dark green crowns. The trees are neatly arranged in rows. They often have small taps near the bottom of the trunk.
NOTE: Rubber trees are common in Thailand. Only use this clue to region-guess if you are certain that you are in Cambodia, and not to identify the country.
clues.summary: Rubber trees have thin trunks and dark green crowns in neat rows, often with small taps near the base. Found in a belt northeast of the capital, around Ban Lung and around Pech Sreada. Common in Thailand too, so use only to place yourself inside the country.

clues.title: Bollard: black-and-white, one road only
text: **Black-and-white bollards** in Cambodia are only found on Road 48, between Tatai and the intersection with Road 4.
NOTE: Make sure to check other clues before guessing, because this style of bollard is commonly found in Thailand.
clues.summary: Black-and-white bollards appear in Cambodia only on Road 48 between Tatai and Road 4. Thailand uses them commonly, so check other clues first.

clues.title: Road: only one side paved, red soil
text: The road between Road 48 and Kiri Sakor is under construction and only has **one paved road side**. The unpaved side has red soil.
clues.summary: The road between Road 48 and Kiri Sakor is under construction, with just one paved side and red soil on the unpaved side.

clues.title: Landscape: red-soil jungle off-roads
text: Several **unpaved jungle offroads** in the southwest of the country, northeast of Road 48, have a distinct look: red soil, dense jungle, and generally hilly terrain.
NOTE: Some rural jungle roads in the east of the country can look similar. Here, however, the soil tends to be more brownish or orange rather than red.
clues.summary: Unpaved jungle tracks in the southwest have red soil, dense jungle and hilly ground. Some eastern jungle roads look similar but with brown or orange soil.

clues.title: Coverage: overcast, big mountains, dirt road
text: The coverage close to **Phnum Samkos** has a distinct look: overcast weather, and large, prominent mountains that are visible in the distance. The roads are unpaved and consist of brown soil. Wild, very green vegetation can be seen all around you.
clues.summary: Near Phnum Samkos: overcast skies, big mountains in the distance, unpaved brown roads and wild, very green vegetation.

clues.title: Bollard: triangular with red stripes
text: Unique **triangular bollards** with red stripes can be found in three places in Cambodia, all located in the same area in the southwest:
- On Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk. They are especially common in the section between Kirirom National Park and Preah Sihanouk.
- One small off-road of Road 4, in Ream National Park near Preah Sihanouk.
- In Preah Monivong National Park.
clues.summary: Triangular bollards with red stripes appear only in the southwest: on Road 4 (mainly Kirirom to Preah Sihanouk), one off-road in Ream National Park, and Preah Monivong National Park.

clues.title: Road: wide red-brown shoulders
text: There is another good way to recognize Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk: in most sections, it has a distinctive **wide, red-brownish shoulder **on both sides of the road.
NOTE: Near Phnom Penh, the soil of these shoulders tends to have a lighter, pinkish or beige colour. In the hills and closer to Preah Sihanouk, the soil tends to have a darker colour.
clues.summary: Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk mostly has wide red-brown shoulders on both sides. Near the capital they are paler, pinkish or beige; in the hills and near the coast they are darker.

clues.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
text: **Oil palm plantations** can only be found on Road 4, as well as some of its rural offroads, just north of Preah Nob.
NOTE: Oil palm plantations are much more common in Malaysia and Indonesia. Only use this clue to region-guess if you are certain that you are in Cambodia, and not to identify the country.
clues.summary: Oil palms only grow on Road 4 and some side roads just north of Preah Nob. They are far more common in Malaysia and Indonesia, so use this only once you know it's Cambodia.

clues.title: Landscape: white rocky plateau, stunted bushes
text: **Preah Monivong National Park** in the south of the country has a unique and recognizable landscape. It is situated on a highland plateau. The soil is white and very rocky. The vegetation consists of stunted, windswept bushes and low trees. The foliage has a distinct dark green tint that contrasts with the white rocks. Some parts of the park are [more forested](https://goo.gl/maps/o8jNzth6g1aK3woh7) but will still have the same rocky soil.
clues.summary: Preah Monivong National Park is a highland plateau with white, very rocky soil and low windswept bushes in a dark green tint. Some parts are more forested but keep the rocky soil.

clues.title: Road: wide grey gravel, runs north-northeast
text: **Road 41**, southwest of Phnom Penh, has a recognizable look and road angle:
- It is a wide road, with a grey and very gravelly road surface
- It runs in a general NNE direction
- The landscape close to the road is flat and agricultural. However, you can often see hills in the distance.
NOTE: There are other roads that can look similar. Therefore, the road angle is very important to identify this road.
clues.summary: Road 41 is wide with a grey, gravelly surface and runs roughly north-northeast. The land beside it is flat farmland, with hills often seen in the distance. Road angle is key since other roads look similar.

clues.title: Pole: three beams, insulators on one side
text: In the sections of Road 6 west of Siem Reap, to Sisophon, and Road 5, south of Sisophon to Krong Battambang, you can find power lines with **unique poles** that are found nowhere else in Cambodia. The pole tops have three horizontal beams, with hanging insulators** on only one side**. The bottom of the poles have [indents](https://goo.gl/maps/HPrch2sJ2uRi862a9).

images.caption: Pole with three beams and insulators on one side; a red box marks the pole top, left

clues.summary: Along Road 6 west of Siem Reap to Sisophon, and Road 5 south of Sisophon to Battambang, poles have three horizontal beams with hanging insulators on one side only, and indents at the bottom. Found nowhere else here.

clues.title: Pole: three beams, insulators on both sides
text: The powerline from the previous tip continues on the section of Road 5 west of Sisophon. However, here the pole tops have insulators **on both sides**. The rest of the pole is identical however.

images.caption: Pole with three beams and insulators on both sides; a red box marks the pole top, left

clues.summary: The same powerline continues on Road 5 west of Sisophon, but the insulators hang on both sides. The rest of the pole is the same.

clues.title: Coverage: overcast, dark tarmac, edge lines
text: The **southern section of Road 76**, south of Krong Saen Monourom, has recognizable coverage: overcast weather, dark asphalt, the presence of outer road lines, and relatively crisp lines for Cambodian standards. Furthermore, a large part of the eastern half of this road runs through hilly terrain with dense jungle.
clues.summary: The southern part of Road 76 has overcast weather, dark asphalt, outer road lines and crisp markings by local standards. Much of the east side runs through hilly dense jungle.

clues.title: Road: wide unpaved brown road in open jungle
text: Most of the **northern section of Road 76**, between Lumphat and Mayura Wild Park, is recognizable too: it is a wide, unpaved road, with brown soil, and a semi-open jungle forest all around you.
Weather conditions start off as overcast on the southern end of the road, and quickly improve the further north you go, with almost completely clear skies on the northern end.
NOTE: There are other, smaller roads that can look similar. However, this road is by far the longest that has this distinct look.
clues.summary: The northern part of Road 76 is a wide unpaved road with brown soil and semi-open jungle all around. Skies are overcast in the south and nearly clear in the north. Other roads can look similar but this is the longest.

clues.title: Sign: Chinese writing next to local script
text: Bilingual signs with **Chinese** writing can commonly be found in Preah Sihanouk.

images.caption: Clinic sign with Chinese writing above the Khmer script

clues.summary: Signs with Chinese writing alongside the local language are common in Preah Sihanouk.

clues.title: Plants: dry-season rubber trees, orange soil
text: Around the town of **Pech Sreada**, in the far east of Cambodia, you can find rubber tree plantations that were covered during the dry season, leading to a distinct look. In addition, the soil is very orange, making it easy to distinguish this area from other regions in Cambodia with rubber tree plantations.
clues.summary: Around Pech Sreada in the far east, rubber plantations were filmed in the dry season, giving them a distinct look, and the soil is very orange.

clues.title: Landmark: dark weathered stone temple complex
text: **Angkor Wat** is a massive temple complex built by the historical Khmer Empire. It is located just north of Siem Reap and has extensive trekker coverage. It can be recognized by its dark, weathered stone buildings. While this location is unlikely to show up in competitive maps, it is extremely common in GeoGuessr’s official Cambodia map.
clues.summary: Angkor Wat, just north of Siem Reap, has a huge complex of dark, weathered stone buildings. It has lots of walking-camera coverage and is common on GeoGuessr's official map, but rare in competitive maps.

clues.title: Sign: stop sign with Khmer and English
text: Stop signs in Cambodia always have the word "Stop" written in Khmer (ឈប់) in addition to the English word.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Stop signs always have the Khmer word (ឈប់) as well as the English word STOP.
